title: Baalbeck festival committee formed under Chamoun
why: President Chamoun named a committee led by Aimée Kettaneh; the event took the name Baalbeck International Festival.

title: New York Philharmonic and Ballet Rambert play Baalbeck
why: Early international acts at the Roman temples placed Lebanon on the Mediterranean festival circuit. (L'Orient Today dates the NY Philharmonic visit to August 1959)

title: Royal Ballet with Margot Fonteyn performs at Baalbeck
why: One of the festival's landmark Western ballet visits in the 1960s.

title: Fonteyn and Nureyev dance at Baalbeck
why: A star pairing at the Temple of Bacchus, a high point of the festival's golden years.

title: Australian Ballet and Moscow Chamber Orchestra at Baalbeck
why: Cold War-era artists from both blocs shared the Baalbeck stage. (festival highlights page lists the Australian Ballet in 1965; Wikipedia also lists the Moscow Chamber Orchestra in 1965)

title: Miles Davis plays Baalbeck, last season before the war
why: The 1973 programme was among the last full seasons before the civil war suspended the festival.

title: Baalbeck festival suspended for the civil war years
why: The festival stayed dark for roughly a quarter century until it reopened in 1997.

title: Baalbeck festival season features Herbie Hancock and Nina Simone
why: The first full programme after the post-war reopening showed international acts returning. (corrected: Wikipedia says the festival reopened in 1997, so 1998 was the second post-war season, not the first)

title: Fairuz's first major hit Itab
why: Composed by Assi Rahbani, it established her as a leading voice in the Arab world.

title: Assi Rahbani suffers a brain haemorrhage
why: His illness shifted composing duties toward his son Ziad and later split the Rahbani-Fairuz partnership.

title: Fairuz separates artistically from the Rahbani brothers
why: The break ended a partnership that defined Lebanese musical theatre.

title: Assi Rahbani dies
why: Co-founder of the Rahbani school of Lebanese song and musical theatre.

title: Fairuz sings in Martyrs' Square for downtown reconstruction
why: A symbolic concert for post-war Beirut's rebuilt centre.

title: Fairuz returns to Baalbeck after 25 years
why: She re-staged old Rahbani musicals with Mansour, Elias and Ziad Rahbani.

title: Fairuz performs at Beiteddine festival
why: Sold-out Beiteddine concerts followed in 2000-2003, anchoring the Chouf festival's profile.

title: Mansour Rahbani dies
why: The surviving Rahbani brother, librettist of the musicals, died in Beirut.

title: Ziad Rahbani born in Antelias
why: Son of Assi Rahbani and Fairuz; became a leading composer and political satirist.

title: Cabinet renames Hafez al-Assad Avenue after Ziad Rahbani
why: Posthumous honour approved days after his death.

title: First local Lebanese film, The Adventures of Elias Mabrouk
why: A silent film directed by Jordano Pidutti, starting local feature production.

title: In the Ruins of Baalbeck becomes first Lebanese sound film
why: Marked the arrival of talking pictures in Lebanese production.

title: Egyptian nationalisation draws filmmakers to Lebanon
why: Filmmakers such as Youssef Chahine relocated, boosting Beirut's studios.

title: Beirut hosts first international film festival in the Arab world
why: Placed Beirut on the regional cinema map before the war.

title: Heiny Srour first Arab woman with a film in Cannes competition
why: Her film was the first by a Lebanese and Arab woman in competition at Cannes.

title: West Beirut is first Arabic-language film released across the US
why: Ziad Doueiri's film brought Lebanese war-era cinema to American cinemas.

title: The Insult is Lebanon's first Oscar nominee
why: Ziad Doueiri's film was nominated for Best Foreign Language Film, the country's first nomination.

title: Capernaum earns an Academy Award nomination
why: Nadine Labaki's film gave Lebanon back-to-back Oscar nominations.

title: L'Orient daily founded in Beirut
why: Founded by Gabriel Khabbaz and Georges Naccache; one of two French dailies that later merged.

title: Le Jour daily founded by Michel Chiha
why: The second French-language daily that later merged with L'Orient.

title: L'Orient-Le Jour first published after merger
why: The merger of L'Orient and Le Jour created Lebanon's main French-language daily.

title: L'Orient editor-in-chief Edouard Saab murdered
why: The editor of L'Orient was killed during the civil war; the paper was briefly shut by Syrian forces that year.

title: An-Nahar founded by Gebran Tueni
why: Started with 500 copies and 50 gold pieces; became Lebanon's leading Arabic daily.

title: An-Nahar closed ten days over a cartoon
why: A government sanction after a controversial cartoon showed press-freedom tensions under the 1960s state.

title: Syrian forces occupy An-Nahar offices
why: An episode of wartime pressure on the Lebanese press.

title: An-Nahar editor Gebran Tueni killed in car bombing
why: The grandson of the founder, an outspoken critic of Syrian influence, was assassinated near Beirut.
dup_of: Gebran Tueni killed by car bomb

title: Ghassan Tueni, long-time An-Nahar publisher, dies
why: He led the paper from 1948 to 1999 and again after his son's death.

title: As-Safir daily launched by Talal Salman
why: An Arab-nationalist daily that became Lebanon's second-largest newspaper.

title: As-Safir ceases publication after 42 years
why: Circulation had fallen below 10,000; a major Arabic daily left the market.

title: The Daily Star founded as English supplement of Al-Hayat
why: Founded by Kamel Mrowa for expatriates; became Lebanon's English daily.

title: The Daily Star restarts after the war
why: Publication resumed after suspensions in 1983-85 and the war years.

title: Daily Star ends its print edition
why: Cited the inability to secure advertising revenue.

title: The Daily Star officially shuts down
why: Online operations suspended on 13 Oct 2021, closing the English daily after unpaid wages and lost ads.

title: Al-Akhbar newspaper founded by Samaha and Al Amin
why: A leftist, Arab-nationalist daily launched by Joseph Samaha and Ibrahim Al Amin.

title: Al-Akhbar publishes WikiLeaks US cables
why: The paper received advance copies; its website was later hacked.

title: STL indicts Al-Akhbar and editor for contempt
why: Special Tribunal for Lebanon contempt case; fined EUR 6,000.

title: First Lebanese radio service begins
why: Public radio began under the Mandate; sources differ, as another page dates Radio Lebanon's origins to 1934.

title: CLT begins broadcasting, first TV station in Lebanon
why: Compagnie Libanaise de Télévision, licensed in August 1956, aired the first TV in the region.
dup_of: CLT begins broadcasting: first commercial TV in the Arab world

title: Press law introduced under President Chehab
why: The 1962 press law still regulated print media in 2013.
dup_of: Press law takes effect under President Chehab

title: New TV launched (later Al Jadeed)
why: Founded by Tahseen Khayat; paused 1997, resumed 2001 and renamed Al Jadeed.

title: Al-Manar begins as a terrestrial channel
why: Hezbollah-owned channel; gained a broadcasting licence in July 1997.

title: Israeli strike demolishes Al-Manar's Baalbek office
why: Cited damage of $52 million.

title: US designates Al-Manar; France bans it from Eutelsat
why: International restrictions on the channel began in late 2004.

title: Future TV starts broadcasting
why: Founded by Rafic Hariri's Future Movement; a major commercial TV player.
dup_of: Future TV starts broadcasting under Rafik Hariri

title: Future TV announces suspension after 26 years
why: Saad Hariri cited financial difficulties after Saudi Oger's collapse.

title: MTV Lebanon shut down
why: Authorities cited breach of the 1999 electoral law; critics saw political motives.

title: MTV Lebanon returns to air
why: Relaunched shortly before the 2009 parliamentary elections.

title: Al Jadeed suspended by Information Minister
why: Chairman arrested for two days; one of several press-freedom episodes.

title: STL acquits Al Jadeed and Karma Khayat of contempt
why: Tribunal acquitted the broadcaster over a witness-protection documentary.

title: Al Mayadeen channel launched in Beirut
why: A pan-Arab news channel based in Lebanon.

title: Elissar Naddaf Geagea becomes first woman to chair Télé Liban
why: First female head of the public broadcaster.

title: Al-Akhbar drops its English section
why: Closed for lack of funds; relaunched May 2025.

title: Gibran's The Prophet published
why: Gibran's English-language book became one of the most translated works of the century.

title: Kahlil Gibran dies in New York
why: His body was moved to Bsharri, where the Gibran Museum stands.

title: Amin Maalouf wins the Prix Goncourt
why: The Rock of Tanios won France's top literary prize.

title: Maalouf wins the Prince of Asturias Award for Literature
why: Recognition for his writing on tolerance and identity.

title: Maalouf elected to the Académie française
why: First person of Lebanese origin to join, taking Claude Lévi-Strauss's seat 29.

title: Maalouf elected Perpetual Secretary of the Académie française
why: A Lebanese-born writer takes the Académie's top administrative post.

title: Etel Adnan publishes Sitt Marie Rose
why: Her war novel won the France-Pays Arabes prize. (corrected from 1977: MERIP review dates the French publication to 1978; Wikipedia says she wrote it in 1977 and sources differ)

title: Etel Adnan shown at documenta 13
why: Marked her late-career rise as a painter.

title: Etel Adnan dies in Paris
why: The Lebanese-American poet and painter died aged 96.

title: Lebanon's first Olympic participation
why: Lebanon first sent athletes to the Summer Games in London.

title: Zakaria Chihab wins Olympic silver in Greco-Roman bantamweight wrestling
why: Silver in Greco-Roman bantamweight wrestling at Helsinki. (corrected: title previously said first Lebanese Olympic medal; insidethegames.biz reports Khalil Taha's bronze came first, the same day)

title: Khalil Taha wins Olympic bronze in wrestling
why: Greco-Roman welterweight bronze at Helsinki. (insidethegames.biz describes Taha as Lebanon's first Olympic medallist)

title: Mohamed Traboulsi wins Olympic weightlifting silver
why: 75 kg silver at Munich, Lebanon's only weightlifting medal.
dup_of: Mohamed Kheir Tarabulsi wins weightlifting silver at Munich

title: Second Pan Arab Games open in Beirut with Lebanon topping medals
why: 914 athletes from 10 countries; Lebanon won 29 gold, 38 silver, 19 bronze.
dup_of: Second Pan Arab Games held in Beirut

title: Beirut hosts the Mediterranean Games
why: First time the Games were held in Asia; 792 athletes from 11 countries, Lebanon 8th with 30 medals.

title: Lebanese Football Association founded
why: One of the first football bodies in the Middle East.

title: Lebanese football league starts as Edmond Rubeiz Cup
why: The origin of today's Lebanese Premier League.

title: Lebanon joins FIFA
why: Membership came three years after the national association was formed.

title: Lebanon plays first international football match
why: A 5-1 loss to Mandatory Palestine; Camille Cordahi scored the first goal.

title: Lebanon plays at EuroBasket 1949
why: Lebanon appeared in EuroBasket in 1949 and 1953.

title: Ansar begin 11 straight Lebanese league titles
why: Their run lasted until 1999.

title: Lebanon hosts AFC Asian Cup
why: Held in Beirut, Sidon and Tripoli; Japan beat Saudi Arabia 1-0 in the final; Lebanon finished last in Group A.
dup_of: Lebanon hosts the AFC Asian Cup

title: Lebanon wins FIBA Asia Cup silver
why: The first of four Asia Cup silver medals.

title: Lebanon wins FIBA Asia Cup silver
why: Second silver in Asia's continental basketball championship.

title: Lebanon wins FIBA Asia Cup silver
why: Third silver in Asia's continental basketball championship.

title: Beirut hosts the Jeux de la Francophonie
why: 46 countries and about 2,500 athletes; Lebanon won 4 silver and 2 bronze.

title: Lebanon hosts FIBA Asia Cup at Nouhad Nawfal Arena
why: Australia won; Lebanon lost to Iran in the semi-final.

title: Lebanon win first Asian Cup match, 4-1 over North Korea
why: Lebanon went out on the fair-play rule at the UAE tournament.

title: Lebanon take FIBA Asia Cup silver; Arakji named MVP
why: Lost the final 73-75 to Australia.

title: Lebanon qualifies for FIBA World Cup after 13 years
why: Finished 23rd overall, then went 1-2 in 2024 Olympic qualifiers.

title: May El-Khalil founds the Beirut Marathon
why: First race drew over 6,000 runners; run by a nonprofit association.

title: Beirut Marathon cancelled over protests
why: Unrest cancelled it; 2020 was suspended for COVID; it returned in 2021.

title: Beirut Marathon returns; Toni Hanna wins men's race
why: A Lebanese winner took the men's title after a two-year gap. (Wikipedia: held 14 Nov 2021, men's winner Toni Hanna, 2:33:03)

title: Lebanese Premier League 2019-20 season cancelled
why: Cancelled amid political and financial crises and COVID-19.

title: Georgina Rizk crowned Miss Lebanon
why: Preceded her Miss Universe win in 1971.

title: Syrian Protestant College renamed American University of Beirut
why: The 1866 college took its present name in 1920.

title: LAU's precursor institution established
why: The Lebanese American University traces its founding to 1924.

title: LAU opens its Byblos campus
why: A second campus 35 km north of Beirut for nursing, medicine, engineering, pharmacy.

title: Student strike and mobilisation leads to Lebanese University
why: A general strike on 23 Jan 1951 preceded creation of the only public university.

title: Car bomb destroys AUB's main administrative building
why: A bombing killed one staff member at the university.

title: AUB restores academic tenure
why: Tenure had been suspended during the civil war.

title: AUB opens Mediterraneo campus in Paphos, Cyprus
why: AUB's first overseas campus.

title: LAU's New York campus becomes degree-granting
why: LAU converted its New York site to a degree-granting campus.

title: National curriculum reform stresses Arabic and national identity
why: The first of three major curriculum reforms (1946, 1968-71, 1997).

title: Curriculum reform reflects rising Pan-Arabism
why: The 1968-71 reform; its history curriculum was never replaced after a 1994 attempt failed.

title: New national curriculum introduced
why: The third major reform of modern Lebanese schooling; not updated after 2000 despite a four-year legal requirement.

title: Cabinet cancels the Brevet official exams for 2020
why: Education Minister Tarek Majzoub announced the cancellation amid COVID-19 closures; baccalaureate fate was announced next day.

title: Peter Medawar shares Nobel Prize in Medicine
why: Born to a father from Jounieh, he won for immunological tolerance; place Abroad.

title: Ardem Patapoutian, born in Beirut, wins Nobel in Medicine
why: Shared the 2021 prize for the discovery of temperature and touch receptors.

title: Michael DeBakey, son of Lebanese immigrants, gets Medal of Freedom
why: The US heart surgeon came from a family from Marjeyoun; Congressional Gold Medal followed in 2008.

title: Elias Hoayek becomes Maronite patriarch
why: Led the Church through the creation of Greater Lebanon in 1920; term ran to 1931. (elected 6 Jan 1899; ratified by Rome 19 June 1899; Wikipedia list gives 1898)

title: Anthony Arida becomes Maronite patriarch
why: Held office until 1955. (corrected from 1931: elected 8 Jan 1932, Hoayek having died Dec 1931)

title: Paul Meouchi becomes Maronite patriarch
why: Later a cardinal; served until 1975. (elected 25 May 1955; died 11 Jan 1975)

title: Antoine Khoraiche becomes Maronite patriarch
why: A cardinal who abdicated in 1986. (elected 3 Feb 1975; resigned 3 April 1986)

title: Nasrallah Sfeir becomes Maronite patriarch
why: He served until 2011 as a cardinal and then Patriarch Emeritus. (elected 19 April 1986; resignation accepted 26 Feb 2011)

title: Bechara Boutros al-Rahi becomes Maronite patriarch
why: Elected 2011; also a cardinal. (elected 15 March 2011; inaugurated 25 March 2011)

title: Beiteddine Festival launched during the war
why: Started in the mid-1980s at Beiteddine Palace as a call for normality.

title: Byblos International Festival begins
why: A July seaside festival in the historic port of Byblos.

title: Abdel Halim Caracalla founds Caracalla Dance Theatre
why: A Beirut company known for folk and theatre-dance productions.

title: Casino du Liban opens
why: The casino and cabaret became a glamour venue of the 1960s.

title: Casino du Liban closes during the civil war
why: Remained shut until 1996.
dup_of: Casino du Liban closes during the war

title: Casino du Liban reopens after $50 million rebuild
why: Reopened after refurbishment.

title: Marcel Khalife founds the Al Mayadine Ensemble
why: The oud player's ensemble toured widely.

title: First prosecution of Marcel Khalife over a Darwish song
why: He faced criminal charges three times, in 1996, 1999 and 2003; he was cleared.

title: Marcel Khalife named UNESCO Artist for Peace
why: Also received the Lebanese Cedar Medal that year.

title: Maroun Bagdadi's Little Wars screens at Cannes
why: The civil-war film brought him international attention.

title: Bagdadi's Out of Life wins Cannes Jury Prize
why: Bagdadi won the Cannes Jury Prize for Out of Life, his best-known recognition.

title: Maroun Bagdadi dies in a fall at his Beirut home
why: He died aged 43 after an elevator-shaft accident.

title: Nadine Labaki's debut Caramel premieres at Cannes
why: Her salon film became an international art-house hit.

title: Sabah born in Bdadoun
why: The singer and actress later made about 98 films.

title: Singer Sabah dies aged 87
why: A leading Arab singer for six decades; funeral at St George Cathedral, Beirut.

title: Wadih El Safi born in Niha
why: The singer later known as Lebanon's 'Immortal Voice'.

title: Wadih El Safi dies aged 91
why: He recorded over 5,000 songs and helped revive folk music through Baalbeck.

title: Composer Zaki Nassif dies in Beirut
why: Known for patriotic songs such as Rajeh Yittammar.

title: Majida El Roumi wins Studio El Fan gold
why: The soprano's breakthrough came at the Lebanese talent show.

title: Majida El Roumi becomes UN and FAO goodwill ambassador
why: Appointed FAO ambassador on World Food Day.

title: Pope Paul VI beatifies Charbel Makhlouf
why: A step toward the sainthood of the Maronite monk, later patron saint of Lebanon.

title: Pope Paul VI canonises Saint Charbel
why: The 19th-century Maronite monk became a saint; he is the patron saint of Lebanon.

title: John Paul II beatifies Nimatullah Kassab
why: A Maronite monk from Hardine, teacher of Saint Charbel.

title: John Paul II canonises Nimatullah Kassab
why: He became patron saint of Beirut.

title: UNESCO lists Anjar, Baalbek, Byblos and Tyre as World Heritage
why: Lebanon's first four sites were inscribed in 1984, during the civil war.

title: Lebanon accepts the UNESCO World Heritage Convention
why: Acceptance came on 30 October 1990.

title: Ouadi Qadisha and the Cedars of God inscribed by UNESCO
why: Lebanon's fifth World Heritage site.
dup_of: Qadisha Valley and Cedars of God inscribed on UNESCO list

title: Rachid Karami International Fair inscribed, listed in danger
why: The Niemeyer fairground in Tripoli was inscribed and flagged as endangered by funding gaps.

title: Mount Amel Castles inscribed as World Heritage in Danger
why: The seventh Lebanese site, listed amid conflict; Tyre was also noted as endangered after 2026 strikes.

title: Al Ahed becomes first Lebanese club to win the AFC Cup
why: Beat April 25 of North Korea 1-0 in the final.

title: Sursock Museum opens in Beirut
why: Opened with an exhibition of contemporary Lebanese artists.

title: Sursock Museum reopens after the port-blast restoration
why: Closed since the 2020 explosion; restoration helped by donors including Italy.

title: National Museum of Beirut officially opens
why: President Alfred Naccache opened the museum after construction from 1930.

title: National Museum partly reopens after the civil war
why: Restoration began in 1995; the museum had stood on the front line.

title: National Museum fully reopens
why: Reopened under President Emile Lahoud's patronage.

title: National Museum opens its underground gallery
why: Showed funerary art from prehistory to the Ottoman era.

title: National Museum reopens after the 2020 blast
why: Reopened with Louvre support.

title: Decree 4116 recognises Notre Dame University-Louaize
why: Gemayel's decree turned the 1978 Louaize college into a university.

title: University of Balamand founded by Patriarch Ignatius IV
why: The Greek Orthodox university started after government clearance in 1988.

title: Sagesse basketball division established
why: Sagesse became a leading club with three FIBA Asia Champions Cup titles and eight Lebanese titles.

title: Paul VI stops in Beirut en route to Bombay
why: First papal visit on Lebanese soil; an hour at the airport welcomed by President Charles Helou.

title: Supreme Islamic Shia Council created under Musa al-Sadr
why: A state-sanctioned Shia body giving the community independent institutional representation.

title: Mohammad Mehdi Shamseddine takes over Shia council
why: Led the council after Musa al-Sadr's disappearance.

title: UNESCO names Beirut World Book Capital 2009
why: Announced 6 July 2007; Beirut became the ninth World Book Capital.

title: Beirut's year as World Book Capital begins
why: Began on World Book and Copyright Day.

title: Lebanon beat France 74-73 at the FIBA World Championship
why: A one-point group-stage win in Sendai, a celebrated result in Lebanese basketball.
dup_of: Lebanon beat France 74-73 at the basketball World Championship

title: Lebanese Basketball Federation founded
why: The governing body for basketball, affiliated with FIBA and FIBA Asia.

title: Lebanon makes its Asian Games debut
why: Lebanon's first gold came in 2002 (Mohammed Anouti, bodybuilding).

title: Mohammed Anouti wins Lebanon's first Asian Games gold
why: Bodybuilding +90 kg at Busan.

title: Jean Claude Rabbath wins Asian Games high-jump gold
why: Doha 2006 was Lebanon's most successful Asian Games. (title corrected from long-jump to high jump: Rabbath is a high jumper, gold at Doha on 9 Dec 2006; Lebanon won one gold and two bronze in 2006)

title: Elie Saab starts his fashion house in Beirut
why: His bridal couture house later became a global brand.

title: Elie Saab dresses Halle Berry for the Oscars
why: First Lebanese designer to dress an Oscar winner.

title: Elie Saab joins Paris Chambre Syndicale de la Haute Couture
why: First Lebanese designer admitted.

title: Mashrou' Leila formed at AUB
why: The indie band became a regional symbol of Lebanese youth culture.

title: Mashrou' Leila's Hamed Sinno unfurls a rainbow flag at Byblos
why: Described as the first public gay pride flag display by a Lebanese artist.

title: Mashrou' Leila first Middle Eastern act on Rolling Stone cover
why: The band's regional profile reached international press.

title: Mashrou' Leila disbands
why: The band cited harassment and hate campaigns.

title: Star Academy Arabia debuts on LBCI
why: The Adma-made reality show drew pan-Arab audiences and ran until 2016.

title: Nancy Ajram breaks through with Akhasmak Ah
why: Her pop hit made her a regional star.

title: Elissa's single Ayshalak breaks through
why: The Lebanese singer's breakthrough single; she signed with Rotana in 2003.

title: Nancy Ajram joins Arab Idol as a judge
why: She sat on the panel from 2013 to 2017.

title: Capernaum nominated for the Oscar for Best Foreign Language Film
why: Labaki became the first Arab woman nominee in the category; Lebanon's second straight nomination after The Insult.

title: Reuters videographer Issam Abdallah killed near Aalma al-Shaab
why: Killed by Israeli tank fire while covering border shelling; UN and rights groups found the strike unlawful or apparently deliberate.
dup_of: Reuters videographer Issam Abdallah killed near the southern border

title: Cabinet cancels official baccalaureate exams over security
why: Students receive certificates from school grades (minimum 9.5/20) after protests and the death of a student in an airstrike. (Arab News dates the Cabinet decision to 25 June 2026; the 9.5/20 minimum was not confirmed on the cited page)

title: Baalbeck festival stages Carmen opera in 2025
why: The festival returned with the theme 'Pillars of Eternity'; a Hiba Tawaji concert followed on 8 August.

title: Lebanon sends 10 athletes to the Paris Olympics
why: Benjamin Hassan gave Lebanon its first Olympic tennis win; no medals.

title: Charles Elachi becomes director of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory
why: Born in Rayak, he led JPL until 30 June 2016; place Abroad.

title: Michael Atiyah, of Lebanese descent, wins the Fields Medal
why: His father was Lebanese; he also won the 2004 Abel Prize; place Abroad.

title: Lebanese inventor Hassan Kamel al-Sabbah dies in a car crash in New York
why: Born in Nabatieh, he held 43 patents, several on television transmission.

title: Radio-East, ancestor of Radio Liban, starts in Beirut
why: Later Radio-Levant and, after 1946, Lebanese Radio; the only legal broadcaster until 1975.

title: NBN television launched by Nabih Berri
why: The channel is tied to the Amal Movement and the Berri family.

title: Lebanese Academy of Fine Arts (ALBA) founded
why: Described as Lebanon's first national institution of higher education; it joined Balamand in 1988.

title: Haigazian College opens in Beirut
why: Founded by Armenian Evangelical bodies with 43 students; became a university in 1996.

title: Beirut Arab University founded by Al-Bir wal-Ihsan Society
why: A private university created by a Lebanese charitable association.

title: Haigazian becomes Haigazian University College
why: Renamed again as Haigazian University in 1996 after ministry authorisation.
